To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a major component (70-90% of total glutamate transport activity) of glutamate transport in cultured rat cortical neurons is dihyrokainate sensitive.

glutamate transport in cortical neurons is mediated by a high affinity dihydrokainic acid-sensitive transporter distinct from EAAC1 and that the dihydrokainatic acid-sensitive transport activity is mediated by GLT1.

a major component (approximately 50%) of high affinity glutamate transporter in rat cortical neurons is a GLT1 transporter, which is insensitive to L-alpha-aminodipate but inhibited by dihydrokainic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
glutamate transport in cultured neurons and in the brain of rats and mice
the identification and characterization of the glutamate uptake systems of rat cortical neurons.

the molecular and cellular biology of the high-affinity glutamate transporter GLT1, which is the predominant glutamate transporter in the central nervous system and which is responsible for the removal of glutamate from the synaptic cleft after neuronal stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high affinity glutamate transporter of rat cortical neurons is a member of the GLT1 family, but is distinct from GLAST and GLT1.

the glutamate transport system is not a single protein, but is a complex system composed of multiple proteins, and that these proteins are differentially regulated and expressed in the central nervous system.
EAAT1 and EAAT2 are astrocytic, EAAT3 is neuronal, EAAT4 and EAAT5 are neuronal and/or glial and EAAT6 is neuronal
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glutamate uptake activity of neurons is a complex phenomenon, with several transporters contributing to the overall activity.
the glutamate transporter GLT1 is expressed by neurons and astrocytes in the CNS, whereas GLAST is expressed only by astrocytes.
EAAC1 is the major glutamate transporter in neurons, whereas GLT1 and GLAST are the major glutamate transporters in astrocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GLT1 is the major transporter in neurons and that it is not inhibited by L-a-aminoadipic acid.
the glutamate transporter GLT1 is present in cortical neurons.
GLT1 is the major glutamate transporter of rat cortical neurons in primary culture.
